# vergeio_network_dns_view (Resource)

`vergeio_network_dns_view` selects which clients receive which zones. Set `network_id` to `vergeio_network.id` so Terraform destroys this view before the network.

`apply` defaults to true and refreshes DNS on a running network after a change. Set `apply` to false on every DNS resource except the last, and make that last one `depends_on` the staged ones, so DNS reloads once. A stopped network is not refreshed. It loads staged DNS when it starts. With `apply` set to false, Terraform leaves `need_dns_apply` set and warns. VergeOS may act on a stale pending flag on its own.

VergeOS deletes the zones and records in this view when the view is deleted. If that delete is refused, Terraform removes the records and zones first so a partial create cannot leave a row that blocks network delete.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One DNS view. apply defaults to true and refreshes DNS after the change.

resource "vergeio_network" "lan" {
  name = "Example LAN"
}

resource "vergeio_network_dns_view" "internal" {
  network_id    = vergeio_network.lan.id
  name          = "internal"
  match_clients = "10.0.0.0/8;"
  recursion     = true
}
```

Stage several DNS resources, then refresh once from the last record.

```terraform
# Stage a view and a zone, then refresh DNS once from the record.

resource "vergeio_network" "lan" {
  name = "Example LAN"
}

resource "vergeio_network_dns_view" "internal" {
  network_id = vergeio_network.lan.id
  name       = "internal"
  apply      = false
}

resource "vergeio_network_dns_zone" "example" {
  view_id = vergeio_network_dns_view.internal.id
  domain  = "example.com"
  type    = "master"
  apply   = false
}

resource "vergeio_network_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_id = vergeio_network_dns_zone.example.id
  host    = "www"
  type    = "A"
  value   = "192.0.2.10"

  depends_on = [
    vergeio_network_dns_view.internal,
    vergeio_network_dns_zone.example,
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) View name, unique on the network.
- `network_id` (String) Network id, the same value as vergeio_network.id. Changing it replaces the view.

### Optional

- `apply` (Boolean) Refresh DNS on this network after the change. Defaults to true. Set false to stage several DNS resources, then leave it true on the last one, which depends_on the others. Each refresh reloads DNS for the whole network. A stopped network is not refreshed. It loads staged DNS when it starts. With apply set to false, Terraform leaves need_dns_apply set and warns. VergeOS may act on a stale pending flag on its own.
- `match_clients` (String) Clients that use this view, in the form VergeOS stores, for example 10.0.0.0/8;192.168.0.0/16;. Omit to leave the current list unchanged.
- `match_destinations` (String) Destinations that use this view, in the same form as match_clients. Omit to leave the current list unchanged.
- `max_cache_size` (Number) Maximum cache size in bytes. 0 means no limit. Omit to leave the current size unchanged.
- `orderid` (Number) Processing order. Lower numbers are checked first. Omit to leave the current order unchanged.
- `query_source` (Number) Address id used as the source of outgoing queries. Omit to leave the current value unchanged.
- `recursion` (Boolean) Allow this view to resolve names it does not serve itself. Omit to leave the current setting unchanged.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) DNS view id.
- `modified` (Number) Last modification time, as seconds since the epoch.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The `terraform import` command can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vergeio_network_dns_view.example <view_id>
```
